_doc_route: Every model is reached through one OpenAI-compatible gateway (OpenRouter), so that the client, the request format, the retry policy and the network path are shared and the model is the only thing that differs between arms - which is what the study claims. `route_direct` is the escape hatch: under ENVIROO_MODEL_ROUTE=direct its fields replace the ones above it, sending the GPT pair straight to api.openai.com on OPENAI_API_KEY. OpenRouter lists openai/gpt-4.1-mini and openai/gpt-5 at the same prices OpenAI does ($0.40/$1.60 and $1.25/$10.00 per 1M, checked 2026-11-06), so the route does not move the cost analysis. It does change what `provider_upstream` records, and a campaign that mixes the two routes is not one campaign - every row carries `model_route` for that reason.
_doc: One model = one OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint. `api_key_env` names the .env variable holding the key (null when the provider needs none, e.g. a local Ollama). Optional per model: `token_param` ('max_tokens' by default, 'max_completion_tokens' for reasoning models that reject the former), `temperature` (a number, or null to omit the parameter entirely - required for models that reject it), `max_output_tokens` (default 4096; higher for reasoning models, which spend part of the budget thinking). Adding a model means adding an entry here; no code changes.
_doc_price: `price_in` / `price_out` = USD per 1 MILLION tokens, used by the benchmark for cost per task. Taken from the providers' pricing pages on 2026-09-05; re-check before a campaign, because a stale price silently mis-states M14. Leave null rather than guessing - with null the cost column stays empty and every other metric is computed normally. Put 0 for locally hosted models.
_doc_study: The four models of the ENVIROO campaign, chosen as two comparable pairs. Closed, hosted: gpt-4.1-mini (cost-efficient tier) vs gpt-5 (top tier), both OpenAI, so the measured variable is the capability tier rather than the vendor. Open-weights, served through OpenRouter: llama-3.3-70b-instruct (large) vs qwen3.5-9b (small enough to run on a single workstation GPU), which is what makes the local-deployment question answerable. The small arm ran on qwen3-8b until the gateway retired that model on 2026-10-09, after which it answered 404; qwen3.5-9b is its successor in the same slot - same vendor lineage, dense (nine billion weights to host, which is what the self-hosting argument rests on, unlike a sparse 35b-a3b) and tool-capable. Runs made on the two are NOT comparable, and the change belongs in the paper rather than only here. Methodological caveat: for the closed models the parameter count is not published, so 'smaller' means the vendor's own declared tier plus its price, not a measured size. temperature=0 wherever the provider accepts it; the GPT-5 family rejects the parameter (400: '`temperature` is deprecated for this model'), so it is sent as null and the run keeps the provider's default sampling - to be reported as a limitation when analysing variance across repetitions.
